My Journey

From caring for people to seeing the bigger picture around care.

Clinical practice teaches you to listen closely — not only to what a patient says, but also to what may be left unsaid. Over time, the questions became broader. Those questions gradually took my work beyond the consultation room — into healthcare services, teams, partnerships and the realities of making healthcare work in the real world. The role has evolved. The perspective has expanded.
  • What happens after treatment?
  • Who supports the family?
  • What happens when care involves several professionals?
  • Why should navigating healthcare become difficult simply because the journey is complex?
The starting point remains simple: understand the person, the context and what the situation actually needs.
I Care

Because healthcare is personal.

A patient experiences care differently from a doctor. A family experiences it differently from an organisation. A caregiver may see a completely different part of the same journey. None of these perspectives tells the whole story.

Good care begins when we make room for all of them. Care is not only about what is delivered — it is also about how people experience it.
I Understand

Healthcare is bigger than the consultation.

A good clinical decision matters. So does everything that makes it possible to follow through — communication, continuity, coordination, support, access, and the systems behind the service. Experience across different sides of healthcare has taught me that the obvious problem is not always the real one.

Sometimes the answer is clinical. Sometimes it is operational. Sometimes it is simply about connecting the right pieces. The distinction matters.
I Connect

Good possibilities often begin with the right people in the room.

Healthcare brings together many capable people and organisations — doctors, specialists, hospitals, care teams, entrepreneurs, institutions. A meaningful connection can open a possibility that did not exist before. Sometimes that means finding expertise. Sometimes it means bringing two complementary capabilities together. Sometimes it simply means knowing who to call.

The right conversation can change what becomes possible.

Neev Healthcare
Restoring Hope at Home.

Neev began in 2022 with a simple intention — to bridge the gap in continuity of care and prevention. Healthcare does not begin at the hospital, and it does not end when treatment is over. A patient may return home with a prescription, but recovery may still need nursing care. A family may need help understanding what comes next.

A person may need physiotherapy to regain independence. Someone may simply need reliable support around them. Today, a team of more than 50 healthcare professionals brings this to more than 1,500 families and counting — with a focus on overall wellbeing that balances modern, advanced care with a genuinely holistic approach.

Care Circle

We all belong to someone's circle of care.

Care is not limited to a profession. It does not belong only to doctors, nurses or professional caregivers. A parent cares for a child. A friend shows up for a friend. A family stands beside someone through a difficult time. Someone helps a stranger. And sometimes, caring begins with learning to be there for ourselves.

Every human being is part of someone's care circle.

Care Circle is a community built around that simple belief — a space where people can come together, share experiences, exchange ideas, express themselves, learn from one another and offer support, without needing a title, achievement or particular role to belong.

A space to give. A space to receive. A space to be.

Care Circle is not a professional network. It is about the human connection underneath our roles — a space for conversations, creativity, learning, connection and simply being around people who understand the value of care.

Different lives. Different stories. One shared human instinct — to care.

Beyond Neev

The work continues across healthcare.

Neev Healthcare is one part of the journey. Alongside it, work is currently underway across areas including occupational health, palliative and hospice care, healthcare education, consulting and strategic partnerships.

Each is at a different stage. Some are being developed independently. Others are taking shape through conversations and collaboration. The details will evolve with the work.

What remains consistent is the intention to find meaningful opportunities where healthcare expertise, capability and purpose can come together. There is room for collaboration where there is genuine alignment.

The Way I Work

Start with the problem. Not the service.

A new service is easy to describe. The harder question is whether it solves the right problem.

  • What is happening? Who is affected?
  • What is missing? What already exists?
  • What would actually make a difference?
  • Can it work in the real world?

The answer may be a new approach. A partnership. A change in process. Or sometimes, a decision not to pursue it.

Good thinking is not about adding more. It is about getting the important things right.

What Matters

Better does not always mean more.

More services do not automatically mean better care. More technology does not automatically mean better healthcare. More people do not automatically mean better outcomes.

Better listening Better communication Better continuity Better coordination

Healthcare improves when the important pieces work better together.

What's Next

There is still more to explore.

Healthcare is changing. The way people live, work and receive care is changing with it — that creates new questions, and new opportunities. The focus ahead is not on doing more for the sake of doing more. It is on finding the spaces where healthcare can become more connected, more practical and more responsive to what people actually need. Some work is already underway. Other possibilities are still taking shape.

The next step does not need every answer. It needs the right question.

Doctor. Founder. Healthcare Entrepreneur.

The titles explain the work. They don't explain the curiosity behind it. Healthcare keeps presenting new questions.

There is always something worth understanding better.
